transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Chinese President Xi is near the end of his state visit to the U.S.
President Trump will take him to the National Archives this morning to see the nation's
founding documents.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Trade Representative Jameson Greer told CNBC today that the U.S. and China
have made progress on some trade issues.
"We want to have some subset of goods that we can trade with the Chinese on a more preferential
basis, where we're sending them ag, we're sending them medical devices, and we're getting
from them consumer goods and other things that are nonsensitive, and we've actually
reached agreement with the Chinese on a number of these things in areas where if we have
trade disputes in the future or if there are tariff measures in the future, we just leave
those things to the side."
He said the Trump administration will release more details on Monday.
President Trump hosted President Xi last night for a state dinner at the White House.
A Democratic senator is asking the White House for immediate answers about a new television
ad featuring the president.
The ad says it's paid for by the U.S. government.
And B.R. Tamara Keith reports the White House insists it is a public service announcement.
The ad features President Trump's voice and a splashy montage of images of the president.
Phrases including largest tax cut in history flash on the screen as the song providing
the soundtrack to the 30-second ad repeats the phrase, "Love me."
"America will never be a communist country."
In a letter demanding answers, Democratic senator from New Hampshire Maggie Hassan says
the ad appears to run afoul of federal prohibitions against using government funds for propaganda.
A White House spokesperson described the ad as a "public service announcement."
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
"The Department of Health and Human Services has nearly $100 million of unspent funding
that is supposed to go to teen pregnancy prevention.
And now there's less than a week to go in the 2026 fiscal year."
This is according to a letter from 92 members of Congress sent to HHS today.
NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin has this exclusive report.
The Democratic Women's Caucus is demanding that the Trump administration restore dozens
of teen pregnancy prevention grants it canceled suddenly in June.
Representative Judy Chu of California is leading the effort.
This is a bipartisan program created by Congress with the clear intent of supporting evidence-based
education models that help reduce teen pregnancy, sexually transmitted diseases, and other health
risks for young people.
She says the Trump administration was trying to unilaterally remake the program to promote
abstinence, but that is not Congress's intent.
A federal judge is also considering a lawsuit brought by grantees that seeks to have the
funding restored.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
California's highest court has ruled that a Republican sheriff illegally seized hundreds
of thousands of ballots earlier this year and must return them.
The ballots were from a vote on whether to redraw California's congressional maps to
favor Democratic candidates.
From member station KVCR, Madison Almond has more.
Sheriff Chad Bianco of Riverside County, about 60 miles east of Los Angeles, said he took
the ballots from the county registrar to investigate alleged voter fraud.
State and county elections officials said there was no evidence of fraud.
California's Attorney General Rob Bonta told Bianco to pause the investigation.
In its rulings, the court says Bianco bypassed election law by taking the ballots and defied
Bonta's authority.
Bonta says the rulings help protect election integrity.
The Riverside County Sheriff is not above the law, and state law must be enforced.
Bianco says he's disappointed by the rulings, but will comply with them.
For NPR News, I'm Madison Almond in San Bernardino.
The National Weather Service is warning a powerful nor'easter storm is winding up to hit part
of the east coast this weekend.
It will target areas from coastal southern Virginia to southern New England.
There could be wind gusts that hit tropical storm strength.
Forecasters are warning there's likely to be significant coastal flooding and a lot of
rain.
Meanwhile, the outer bands of Hurricane NOLO are starting to reach the big island of Hawaii.
A hurricane watches up.
Forecasters don't think the storm will make landfall, but it is quite a rainmaker.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.
This week on the NPR Politics Podcast, Republicans are on their heels and about to spend a lot
of money on ads.
Some of these ads are going to be ugly, and it's going to be a pretty negative campaign.
That's the nature of a midterm when you've got an environment like the one that the Republicans
are facing.
We look at the Republican money machine with less than 40 days until the midterms.
This week on the NPR Politics Podcast.

topics.text: Chinese President Xi near end of state visit to U.S., Trump to show founding documents
U.S. Trade Representative says progress made on trade issues with China, details Monday
Trump hosted state dinner for Chinese President Xi at White House last night
Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan questions White House ad featuring Trump paid by government
HHS has nearly $100 million unspent teen pregnancy prevention funding with week left in fiscal year
Democratic Women's Caucus demands Trump administration restore dozens of canceled teen pregnancy prevention grants
Federal judge considering lawsuit to restore teen pregnancy prevention funding from grantees
California court rules Republican Sheriff Chad Bianco illegally seized ballots, must return them
Powerful nor'easter storm to hit east coast this weekend from Virginia to New England
Outer bands of Hurricane Nolo reaching Hawaii's Big Island, significant rainfall expected
